Your Google reviews are written on your worst day, not your average one.

Here’s why, and it’s not your service.

An unhappy customer goes home angry.
Anger is a great motivator.
They write the review that night.

A happy customer goes home happy.
Happy people make dinner.
They watch something.
They forget.
They meant to leave you five stars.

Nobody reminded them.

So your page fills up with the few who were upset, while the many who loved you stay silent.

That’s not a reputation problem.

It’s an asking problem.

The fix is boring:
Ask every happy customer, within a few hours, while the feeling is fresh.

Make it one tap. The link, not “find us on Google.”

Do it every time, not when someone remembers.

Good work doesn’t speak for itself. Someone has to ask it to.

Today, ask your team one question: “Who sends the review request, and when?”
If the answer is “whoever remembers,” it’s nobody.
